passages.text: “If someone sins by failing to testify when he hears a public charge about something he has witnessed, whether he has seen it or learned of it, he shall bear the iniquity.
passages.sermon:
A person may sin.
He may hear a public charge.
He may be a witness.
He may have seen the event.
He may have learned about it.
If he does not testify,
He will bear his guilt.
passages.original: וְנֶ֣פֶשׁ כִּֽי־ תֶחֱטָ֗א וְשָֽׁמְעָה֙ ק֣וֹל אָלָ֔ה וְה֣וּא עֵ֔ד א֥וֹ רָאָ֖ה א֣וֹ יָדָ֑ע אִם־ ל֥וֹא יַגִּ֖יד וְנָשָׂ֥א עֲוֺנֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Or if a person touches anything unclean—whether the carcass of any unclean wild animal or livestock or crawling creature—even if he is unaware of it, he is unclean and guilty.
passages.sermon:
A person may touch something unclean.
He may touch the dead body of an unclean wild animal.
He may touch the dead body of unclean livestock.
He may touch the dead body of an unclean crawling creature.
He may not know that he touched something unclean.
But he is still unclean.
He is guilty.
passages.original: א֣וֹ נֶ֗פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּגַּע֮ בְּכָל־ דָּבָ֣ר טָמֵא֒ אוֹ֩ בְנִבְלַ֨ת חַיָּ֜ה טְמֵאָ֗ה א֤וֹ בְּנִבְלַת֙ בְּהֵמָ֣ה טְמֵאָ֔ה א֕וֹ בְּנִבְלַ֖ת שֶׁ֣רֶץ טָמֵ֑א וְנֶעְלַ֣ם מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְה֥וּא טָמֵ֖א וְאָשֵֽׁם׃

passages.text: Or if he touches human uncleanness—anything by which one becomes unclean—even if he is unaware of it, when he realizes it, he is guilty.
passages.sermon:
A person may touch something that makes a human unclean.
This can be any way that a person becomes unclean.
At first, the person may not know he touched it.
Later, the person learns what he did.
That person is guilty.
passages.original: א֣וֹ כִ֤י יִגַּע֙ בְּטֻמְאַ֣ת אָדָ֔ם לְכֹל֙ טֻמְאָת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִטְמָ֖א בָּ֑הּ וְנֶעְלַ֣ם מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְה֥וּא יָדַ֖ע וְאָשֵֽׁם׃

passages.text: Or if someone swears thoughtlessly with his lips to do anything good or evil—in whatever matter a man may rashly pronounce an oath—even if he is unaware of it, when he realizes it, he is guilty in the matter.
passages.sermon:
A person may make a careless promise with his mouth.
He may promise to do something bad or something good.
He may make any kind of oath that people speak.
He may not realize what he has done at first.
Later, he learns about it.
He is guilty for what he has promised.
passages.original: א֣וֹ נֶ֡פֶשׁ כִּ֣י תִשָּׁבַע֩ לְבַטֵּ֨א בִשְׂפָתַ֜יִם לְהָרַ֣ע׀ א֣וֹ לְהֵיטִ֗יב לְ֠כֹל אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְבַטֵּ֧א הָאָדָ֛ם בִּשְׁבֻעָ֖ה וְנֶעְלַ֣ם מִמֶּ֑נּוּ וְהוּא־ יָדַ֥ע וְאָשֵׁ֖ם לְאַחַ֥ת מֵאֵֽלֶּה׃

passages.text: If someone incurs guilt in one of these ways, he must confess the sin he has committed, and he must bring his guilt offering to the LORD for the sin he has committed: a female lamb or goat from the flock as a sin offering. And the priest will make atonement for him concerning his sin.
passages.sermon:
A person may become guilty by doing one of these things.
He must admit the sin he has done.
He must bring an offering to the LORD for his sin.
He must bring a female lamb or a female goat from the flock.
This animal will be a sin offering.
The priest will make atonement for him for his sin.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֥ה כִֽי־ יֶאְשַׁ֖ם לְאַחַ֣ת מֵאֵ֑לֶּה וְהִ֨תְוַדָּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָטָ֖א עָלֶֽיהָ׃ וְהֵבִ֣יא אֶת־ אֲשָׁמ֣וֹ לַיהוָ֡ה עַ֣ל חַטָּאתוֹ֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר חָטָ֜א נְקֵבָ֨ה מִן־ הַצֹּ֥אן כִּשְׂבָּ֛ה אֽוֹ־ שְׂעִירַ֥ת עִזִּ֖ים לְחַטָּ֑את וְכִפֶּ֥ר עָלָ֛יו הַכֹּהֵ֖ן מֵחַטָּאתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: If, however, he cannot afford a lamb, he may bring to the LORD as restitution for his sin two turtledoves or two young pigeons—one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering.
passages.sermon:
A person may sin and become guilty before the LORD.
He must bring an offering for his sin.
If he cannot afford a lamb, he must bring two birds to the LORD.
He may bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons.
He must bring one bird as a sin offering.
He must bring the other bird as a burnt offering.
passages.original: וְאִם־ לֹ֨א תַגִּ֣יע יָדוֹ֮ דֵּ֣י שֶׂה֒ וְהֵבִ֨יא אֶת־ אֲשָׁמ֜וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטָ֗א שְׁתֵּ֥י תֹרִ֛ים אֽוֹ־ שְׁנֵ֥י בְנֵֽי־ יוֹנָ֖ה לַֽיהוָ֑ה אֶחָ֥ד לְחַטָּ֖את וְאֶחָ֥ד לְעֹלָֽה׃

passages.text: He is to bring them to the priest, who shall first present the one for the sin offering. He is to twist its head at the front of its neck without severing it; then he is to sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the altar, while the rest of the blood is drained out at the base of the altar. It is a sin offering.
passages.sermon:
A person brings two birds to the priest as an offering for sin.
The priest takes the birds.
The priest presents the first bird as a sin offering.
The priest twists the head of the first bird at the front of its neck.
The priest does not sever the head from the body.
The priest sprinkles some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the altar.
The priest drains the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
This is a sin offering.
passages.original: וְהֵבִ֤יא אֹתָם֙ אֶל־ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְהִקְרִ֛יב אֶת־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לַחַטָּ֖את רִאשׁוֹנָ֑ה וּמָלַ֧ק אֶת־ רֹאשׁ֛וֹ מִמּ֥וּל עָרְפּ֖וֹ וְלֹ֥א יַבְדִּֽיל׃ וְהִזָּ֞ה מִדַּ֤ם הַחַטָּאת֙ עַל־ קִ֣יר הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וְהַנִּשְׁאָ֣ר בַּדָּ֔ם יִמָּצֵ֖ה אֶל־ יְס֣וֹד הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ חַטָּ֖את הֽוּא׃

passages.text: And the priest must prepare the second bird as a burnt offering according to the ordinance. In this way the priest will make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and he will be forgiven.
passages.sermon:
The priest prepares the second bird as a burnt offering.
The priest follows the required instructions.
The priest makes atonement for the man.
The man has sinned.
The priest acts because of the man's sin.
God forgives the man.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ הַשֵּׁנִ֛י יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה עֹלָ֖ה כַּמִּשְׁפָּ֑ט וְכִפֶּ֨ר עָלָ֧יו הַכֹּהֵ֛ן מֵחַטָּאת֥וֹ אֲשֶׁר־ חָטָ֖א וְנִסְלַ֥ח לֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: But if he cannot afford two turtledoves or two young pigeons, he may bring a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a sin offering. He must not put olive oil or frankincense on it, because it is a sin offering.
passages.sermon:
A person may sin and need to bring a sin offering.
Sometimes a person cannot afford two turtledoves.
Sometimes a person cannot afford two young pigeons.
If he cannot afford these birds, he may bring fine flour instead.
He must bring a tenth of an ephah of fine flour.
He brings this flour as his sin offering.
He must not put olive oil on the flour.
He must not put frankincense on the flour.
This is because it is a sin offering.
passages.original: וְאִם־ לֹא֩ תַשִּׂ֨יג יָד֜וֹ לִשְׁתֵּ֣י תֹרִ֗ים אוֹ֮ לִשְׁנֵ֣י בְנֵי־ יוֹנָה֒ וְהֵבִ֨יא אֶת־ קָרְבָּנ֜וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטָ֗א עֲשִׂירִ֧ת הָאֵפָ֛ה סֹ֖לֶת לְחַטָּ֑את לֹא־ יָשִׂ֨ים עָלֶ֜יהָ שֶׁ֗מֶן וְלֹא־ יִתֵּ֤ן עָלֶ֙יהָ֙ לְבֹנָ֔ה כִּ֥י חַטָּ֖את הִֽיא׃

passages.text: He is to bring it to the priest, who shall take a handful from it as a memorial portion and burn it on the altar atop the offerings made by fire to the LORD; it is a sin offering.
passages.sermon:
A man brings his offering to the priest.
The offering is fine flour for a sin offering.
The priest takes a handful of the flour.
This handful is called the memorial portion.
The priest burns the memorial portion on the altar.
He burns it on top of the offerings made by fire to the LORD.
This offering is a sin offering.
passages.original: וֶהֱבִיאָהּ֮ אֶל־ הַכֹּהֵן֒ וְקָמַ֣ץ הַכֹּהֵ֣ן׀ מִ֠מֶּנָּה מְל֨וֹא קֻמְצ֜וֹ אֶת־ אַזְכָּרָתָה֙ וְהִקְטִ֣יר הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חָה עַ֖ל אִשֵּׁ֣י יְהוָ֑ה חַטָּ֖את הִֽוא׃

passages.text: In this way the priest will make atonement for him for any of these sins he has committed, and he will be forgiven. The remainder will belong to the priest, like the grain offering.”
passages.sermon:
The priest makes atonement for the person.
The person has sinned.
The person has committed one of these sins.
The priest acts on behalf of the person.
God forgives the person.
The priest receives the remainder of the offering.
The priest receives it as he receives the grain offering.
passages.original: וְכִפֶּר֩ עָלָ֨יו הַכֹּהֵ֜ן עַל־ חַטָּאת֧וֹ אֲשֶׁר־ חָטָ֛א מֵֽאַחַ֥ת מֵאֵ֖לֶּה וְנִסְלַ֣ח ל֑וֹ וְהָיְתָ֥ה לַכֹּהֵ֖ן כַּמִּנְחָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “If someone acts unfaithfully and sins unintentionally against any of the LORD’s holy things, he must bring his guilt offering to the LORD: an unblemished ram from the flock, of proper value in silver shekels according to the sanctuary shekel; it is a guilt offering.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
He gave Moses instructions.
If a person acts unfaithfully against the LORD’s holy things, he has sinned.
If he sins unintentionally, he is still guilty.
He must bring a guilt offering to the LORD.
He must bring an unblemished ram from his flock.
The ram must be of proper value.
He must value the ram in silver shekels.
He must use the sanctuary shekel for this value.
This offering is a guilt offering.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ נֶ֚פֶשׁ כִּֽי־ תִמְעֹ֣ל מַ֔עַל וְחָֽטְאָה֙ בִּשְׁגָגָ֔ה מִקָּדְשֵׁ֖י יְהוָ֑ה וְהֵבִיא֩ אֶת־ אֲשָׁמ֨וֹ לַֽיהוָ֜ה אַ֧יִל תָּמִ֣ים מִן־ הַצֹּ֗אן בְּעֶרְכְּךָ֛ כֶּֽסֶף־ שְׁקָלִ֥ים בְּשֶֽׁקֶל־ הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ לְאָשָֽׁם׃

passages.text: Regarding any holy thing he has harmed, he must make restitution by adding a fifth of its value to it and giving it to the priest, who will make atonement on his behalf with the ram as a guilt offering, and he will be forgiven.
passages.sermon:
If a person has sinned against any of the LORD’s holy things, he must pay back what he has taken or harmed.
He must add one fifth of its value to the amount.
He must give this total amount to the priest.
The priest will take a ram as a guilt offering.
The priest will make atonement for the person with the ram.
The person will be forgiven.
passages.original: וְאֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר֩ חָטָ֨א מִן־ הַקֹּ֜דֶשׁ יְשַׁלֵּ֗ם וְאֶת־ חֲמִֽישִׁתוֹ֙ יוֹסֵ֣ף עָלָ֔יו וְנָתַ֥ן אֹת֖וֹ לַכֹּהֵ֑ן וְהַכֹּהֵ֗ן יְכַפֵּ֥ר עָלָ֛יו בְּאֵ֥יל הָאָשָׁ֖ם וְנִסְלַ֥ח לֽוֹ׃פ

passages.text: If someone sins and violates any of the LORD’s commandments even though he was unaware, he is guilty and shall bear his punishment.
passages.sermon:
A person may sin.
This person may break one of the LORD’s commandments.
These commandments are things the LORD said not to do.
The person may not know he has sinned.
He is still guilty.
He must bear his punishment.
passages.original: וְאִם־ נֶ֙פֶשׁ֙ כִּ֣י תֶֽחֱטָ֔א וְעָֽשְׂתָ֗ה אַחַת֙ מִכָּל־ מִצְוֺ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר לֹ֣א תֵעָשֶׂ֑ינָה וְלֹֽא־ יָדַ֥ע וְאָשֵׁ֖ם וְנָשָׂ֥א עֲוֺנֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He is to bring to the priest an unblemished ram of proper value from the flock as a guilt offering. Then the priest will make atonement on his behalf for the wrong he has committed in ignorance, and he will be forgiven.
passages.sermon:
The person has sinned by breaking one of the LORD’s commandments without knowing it.
He must bring a ram to the priest.
The ram must be unblemished.
The ram must come from his flock.
The ram must be of proper value.
He brings the ram as a guilt offering.
The priest receives the ram.
The priest makes atonement for the person.
The priest does this because the person sinned in ignorance.
The person did not know he sinned.
After the atonement, God forgives the person.
passages.original: וְ֠הֵבִיא אַ֣יִל תָּמִ֧ים מִן־ הַצֹּ֛אן בְּעֶרְכְּךָ֥ לְאָשָׁ֖ם אֶל־ הַכֹּהֵ֑ן וְכִפֶּר֩ עָלָ֨יו הַכֹּהֵ֜ן עַ֣ל שִׁגְגָת֧וֹ אֲשֶׁר־ שָׁגָ֛ג וְה֥וּא לֹֽא־ יָדַ֖ע וְנִסְלַ֥ח לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: It is a guilt offering; he was certainly guilty before the LORD.”
passages.sermon: This is a guilt offering.\r\nThe person is guilty.\r\nHe is guilty before the LORD.
